title: Emergent Misalignment at Different Model Scales Within One Family

original_idea.body:
# Emergent Misalignment at Different Model Scales Within One Family

**Problem:** The 12-model replication found a correlation between model size and emergent misalignment susceptibility, but it spanned families. A clean within-family scale sweep would isolate scale from architecture as the driver.

**Direction:** Apply the identical insecure-code LoRA fine-tune to multiple sizes of one open family (e.g., Qwen2.5 0.5B / 1.5B / 7B) and measure broad-misalignment rate vs size on the standard eval. Twist: hold family/data/recipe fixed and vary only scale to test the reported size-susceptibility correlation.

**Why it matters:** If misalignment susceptibility grows with scale within a family, it predicts the problem worsens as open models grow, a clean medium-horizon warning sign. The experiment is entirely consumer-GPU feasible with LoRA and needs no proprietary data.

**Relevant context:** The 12-model replication (arXiv:2506.11613) reports a significant correlation between model size and emergent misalignment, but conflates family and scale. Betley et al. (arXiv:2502.17424) provide the recipe and eval. Qwen2.5 family spans 0.5B-72B openly.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible scale-warning chain but indirect to catastrophic risk; a skipped step.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Identical LoRA finetune across 3 sizes + eval; guided and inheritable.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open family, no proprietary data; diffuse scale-trend work.

low_compute.reasoning: Three small LoRA finetunes (7B is the largest); feasible.

novelty.reasoning: Size correlation noted across families; clean within-family isolation may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Cross-family correlation shown; within-family isolation may be open.
